# Long Read

A long document for practising section-by-section reading. Collapse all
headings with `H` to turn it into an outline, then expand one chapter at a
time to keep your place.

## Chapter 1: The reading desk

The reading desk is where every document opens. The sidebar on the left keeps
the library within reach, and the status strip below the reader reports the
line count of the current document.

### 1.1 Layout

The desk has three regions. The sidebar can be resized by dragging its edge,
collapsed to a thin strip, and restored with the keyboard.

### 1.2 Zoom

Application zoom changes the size of everything in the window. The reader
keeps its margins and line length under all zoom levels.

## Chapter 2: Sections

Documents are divided into sections at every heading. A section contains its
heading and everything up to the next heading of the same or higher level.

### 2.1 Nesting

Sections nest. Collapsing a chapter hides its subsections; expanding the
chapter reveals the subsection headings, which can then be collapsed
individually.

### 2.2 State

The reader remembers which sections you collapsed per document while the app
is open, so you can switch documents and return without losing your place.

## Chapter 3: Reading strategies

Reading a large document in one pass is hard. Collapsing the outline first
gives you a map, and expanding one section at a time keeps each reading
session short and focused.

### 3.1 One section at a time

Expand a single heading, read to its end, collapse it again, and move to the
next heading. The visible outline acts as a bookmark.

### 3.2 Finishing the document

When every section has been read, expand everything with `L` and skim the
result to confirm nothing was skipped.
